raw.assessment: The incumbent supports routine cases: unchanged-assignment exports had a seven-minute median handling time, a concrete limit on any claim that scheduled CSV generation is inherently inadequate (D1-O2). Overall, only 32/40 had the intended courses and handling took 17 minutes (D1-O1/O2). Assignment changes and renames concentrate among affected exports, but do not establish causation (D1-O3). Fast generation alongside long replacement waits suggests a separate delay worth measuring (D1-O5). Zero observed cross-center rows does not establish isolation for the omitted split-course center (D1-O4). No proposed change yet demonstrates the next-40-export targets.

openings.claim: Using current instructor assignments may select the wrong course membership for a requested week; renamed courses may instead create recognition errors in otherwise complete files.
openings.delta: Distinguishes incorrect exported membership from correct membership that coordinators cannot recognize.
openings.prediction: With attendance and intended membership fixed, reassignment changes emitted membership if selection is time-dependent; a recognition explanation predicts correct records with additional coordinator checking after renaming.
openings.probe: In staging, compare fabricated unchanged, reassigned and renamed courses against a predeclared weekly membership list. Have consenting coordinators identify each course. Consider week-aware selection or clearer identity presentation only after distinguishing these outcomes.
assumptions: Relevant historical assignments or identifiers may be unavailable.
Any implementation must retain the CSV schema, private processing and attendance entry, and fit six engineer-days and existing hosting.

openings.claim: Does replacement delay chiefly precede job start, or follow job completion through delivery, correction or import?
openings.delta: Separates actionable queue or delivery delay from coordinator handling time; elapsed waiting is not evidence of active work.
openings.prediction: Queue delay concentrates before job start; delivery delay follows completion; checking or import friction increases measured active minutes after receipt.
openings.probe: Use the two short sessions per consenting coordinator to rehearse fabricated replacement requests and timestamp request, start, completion, receipt and active handling within existing private tools. Include one split-course fixture with a declared center boundary and verify every exported row.
assumptions: Staging timings distinguish stages but may not represent production queues.
Fabricated sessions consume only the bounded investigation budget and leave ordinary attendance entry available.

raw.assessment: Assignment changes and renames coincide with affected exports, but causation is unproven. Replacement delay greatly exceeds execution time. The sample neither establishes isolation for split courses nor separates checking from importing effort. Both openings are bounded hypotheses requiring effort and hosting checks.

openings.claim: Attendance entries may provide an independent witness of courses belonging to the requested week when current assignments or names mislead export selection. Privately compare distinct center-scoped course IDs on that week's entries against selected export courses and surface disagreements to the coordinator.
openings.delta: Detect selection errors through historical activity rather than relying exclusively on current administrative labels or each coordinator's timetable.
openings.prediction: If this explanation holds, fabricated reassignment and rename cases retain attendance-linked course IDs absent from export selection; unchanged controls do not. Zero-entry intended courses expose the witness's coverage limit.
openings.probe: In staging, compare selections with attendance-linked IDs for unchanged, reassigned, renamed, split, and zero-entry courses. Obtain intended sets from consenting coordinators. Test center ownership on every lookup and nonblocking reads while entering attendance; preserve the documented CSV.
assumptions: Entries preserve usable course and week identifiers.
Disagreements support review, not automatic inclusion or proof of completeness.
A bounded implementation fits six engineer-days and existing hosting.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: an authenticated coordinator correction-and-regenerate action could remove the replacement queue. Let coordinators confirm the week and intended course IDs within their authorized center, then run the existing CSV exporter immediately.
openings.delta: Move correction authority to the coordinator at discovery time, reducing dependence on a separately handled replacement request.
openings.prediction: Ready-file latency falls substantially, but handling time improves only if correction requests and repeat checking account for meaningful active effort.
openings.probe: Use counterbalanced fabricated tasks in the two coordinator sessions. Compare existing replacement handling with a staging regeneration control; measure active checking, correction, download/import time, ready-file latency, and intended-set accuracy separately. Reject foreign-center course IDs server-side and verify attendance entry continues during export.
assumptions: Existing export selection can accept explicit authorized course IDs.
Bounded reruns fit hosting capacity and six engineer-days.
Reduced waiting alone does not establish the twelve-minute handling target.

critiques.assumption: Coordinator-declared intended sets are sufficiently reliable to evaluate attendance-based detection and coordinator-directed regeneration.
critiques.limitation: D1-O6 establishes heterogeneous schedule sources, while timetable completeness and update timing are explicitly unmeasured. This supports an untested reference standard, not a claim that any coordinator is wrong. A1 already acknowledges zero-entry coverage limits; combining it with A2 still leaves both completeness and added review effort unresolved.
critiques.opening: Test disagreement-directed correction against independently authored scenario truth, including a deliberately stale timetable, before treating coordinator confirmation as evidence of correctness.
critiques.comparison: A1 detects activity-selection discrepancies without fixing selection; A2 enables correction without identifying where attention is needed. Their proposed interaction directs correction toward discrepancies. Z1 supplies the separate membership-versus-recognition diagnosis. Failure occurs when intended courses have no entries, identifiers change, or both displayed sources share the same omission.
critiques.probe: Proposed only: fabricated cases with predetermined intended sets, crossed with accurate and stale timetable cues. Score final exports against scenario truth and record false confirmations, unresolved cases, and active minutes. No world tests were performed.

openings.claim: A private discrepancy review linked to authorized regeneration may reduce correction effort while making unresolved coverage visible.
openings.delta: Join A1 detection to A2 correction, retain Z1 diagnosis, and prevent agreement between incomplete sources from being presented as verified completeness.
openings.prediction: Compared with A2 alone, known discrepancies should take less checking; compared with A1 alone, fewer requests should need separate replacement handling. Added review may instead increase handling time. Zero-entry omissions remain a failure boundary.
openings.probe: Proposed: use six coordinators in two short counterbalanced fabricated sessions to compare both parents and the hybrid. Include reassignment, rename, split and zero-entry cases; measure active handling separately from latency. Reject foreign-center IDs and exercise concurrent attendance entry.
openings.fit: Preserves outcome and constraints conditionally; the next-40 targets remain unverified. Retain private processing and documented CSV, with six-day and hosting feasibility checked before implementation.
assumptions: Stable center-scoped course/week identifiers and an exporter accepting authorized explicit IDs are unverified dependencies.
Smallest assessable capability: a fabricated discrepancy panel feeding one authorized staging regeneration, with an explicit unresolved-coverage state.
